entries.test: Public evidence about competing AI firms’ technologies, training data, and durable competitive advantages would establish whether shared technology and data leave all of them without a moat.
entries.note: “Moat” has a conventional business meaning: a durable competitive advantage.

entries.test: If the AI market has no clear winners, public pricing, margin, and competition data would show whether firms lack monopoly pricing power and experience price wars and commodity pricing.
entries.note: The forecast explicitly depends on the absence of clear winners and supplies no deadline.

entries.test: AI companies’ disclosed investment costs and subsequent profits would show whether all ultimately spent more than their financial returns justified in the predicted competitive market.
entries.note: He presents intense competition as the expected outcome of his argument, rather than a separate hypothetical. No deadline is given.

“The economics don’t make sense” supplies no shared criterion for judging the industry’s economics. The increasing attention component is empirically assessable, but does not settle the whole proposition.
